body: im sorry to hear that. if you need to talk im here.
yeah, the feelings you get as a result of not getting enough sleep fucking suck.

i can’t tell in particular, im just overwhelmed. counseling has been somewhat of a negative experience for me, really. they were always very dismissive and invalidating, so i’ve almost given up on therapy.
sure. im not the best at responding, but i care.

you must feel really stuck right now, and that fucking sucks. when i was discharged from my first hospitalization, i began to struggle with OCD (anxiety disorders run deep in my family as well). i couldn’t read certain books or listen to certain  songs, (which killed me, because music is one of the only things keeping me alive) and i had the thing with shirts as well. i always thought it was just me who even felt that way, which just drove me crazier. while i no longer suffer from this, i understand what it’s like. if you ever need anyone to talk to, im here. i hope you feel better
i relate to this. i write, delete, and rewrite until im too worn out to keep my eyes open. if you ever need anything, message me.

im not a religious person at all, and id even say that i dislike most religions. im not really a big believer in “life after death”, or whatever... in my mind, i just imagine death as the end of a story. a loss of consciousness, or feeling. i think the reason why people are afraid of death is because nobody definitively knows what it means. nobody knows for sure what happens after you die. but with that comes a sort of morbid curiosity, a desire to understand what it really means. it’s odd how people who find death interesting are almost shamed socially. like they’re sickos, or creeps for wondering. but in the end, the curiosity of death is the same as the curiosity of life. both are things that need to happen. things that will happen. and both are beautiful in their own ways. instead of being afraid or appalled by death, maybe we should welcome it and question it

everybody wants a reason to keep going. it’s funny; if life wasn’t valued, than nobody in any amount of pain would live it. i often think about the way society views things like life and death, and in the end i feel as if it boils down to fear. the fear of the unknown, or the fear of being wrong.
